document_title: Who watches Alaska's fishing boats in 2027
post_copy:
In 2027 camera hardware moves into Alaska's fisheries monitoring budget while the AI that could review the video waits on staff.

Who pays for the camera? Congress has, since 2023. That money is expected to run out this year. The draft puts hardware at $6,002.96 a year per fixed-gear camera boat, inside a preliminary $5.45M budget.

Will your trip get picked? In the draft an observer rides 31.35 percent of Bering Sea and Aleutian fixed-gear trips and 9.31 percent in the Gulf. Under 40 feet, nobody is chosen.

Who watches your footage? A review provider, priced per hard drive reviewed. NMFS lists the AI project for 2027 "pending availability of staff resources."

The slides show the budget, draft odds for all ten strata and the AI line as printed.

How much of that $5.45M should reach the AI review line before more cameras go aboard?

#AlaskaFisheries #ElectronicMonitoring #NOAAFisheries

slides.headline:
This camera watches an Alaska fishing boat.
Who watches the footage?

One review provider,
priced by the hard drive.
slides.body: NMFS prices camera review by the hard drive, a year of review spending divided by drives reviewed. The program currently has one EM review provider.

slides.headline:
Congress paid for the cameras.
That money is expected to end this year.
slides.body: Since 2023, Congressional Directed Spending covered new EM systems and replacements. With it spent by the end of 2026, the 2027 plan carries that cost itself, about $6,002.96 a year per fixed-gear camera boat.

slides.headline:
A preliminary $5.45M,
with cameras off the top.
slides.body: Trawl cameras come off the top at $732K. About $4.72M is left for observers and fixed-gear cameras, subject to change.
labels: ONE CAMERA BOAT'S HARDWARE, $6,002.96, THIS WIDE

slides.headline: Nobody is chosen.
slides.body: Boats under 40 feet and jig boats have no chance of carrying an observer or a camera in 2027. The draft expects 1,427 such trips.

slides.headline:
Some trips still
carry a person.
slides.body: In the draft, an observer rides 79 of 253 expected fixed-gear trips in the Bering Sea and Aleutians, 31.35 percent. In the Gulf it is 174 of 1,868, or 9.31 percent.

slides.headline: Who gets watched in 2027.
labels: PRELIMINARY RATES. FINAL PLAN TO THE COUNCIL IN DECEMBER. BSAI IS BERING SEA AND ALEUTIANS.

the video is on a list.
slides.body: NMFS intends to support it in 2027, "pending availability of staff resources." The title is in the draft. The staffing is pending.

editor_notes_for_email: Caption carried byte for byte, and no slide strings needed changes. Two notes for the showrunner. The hook says camera hardware moves into the 2027 budget, but in this draft only the fixed-gear camera cost includes equipment. Trawl camera equipment moves over in the Final ADP (C09 notes, lines 580 to 582), so the hook is accurate for the plan as a whole and loose for this draft. Slide 3 keeps "by the end of 2026" because the year is set against the 2027 plan, not used as a date. Rates and the $5.45M are preliminary throughout. The AI project has no named lead or funder in the draft, and nothing here ties it to ALFA's FishVue.
